projection_notice: Curator paraphrases of selected primary-source facts; not a verbatim article or an independent scientific validation. Exact sections must be checked against the cited source during review.

facts: Biomass from 96-hour Fusarium sp. BI cultures supplied with 1.5 mM bismuth subsalicylate or 1.5 mM salicylate was washed and prepared for microscopy.
Approximately 60 nm sections were examined by TEM with energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy.
Bi signal was localized with phosphorus-rich intracellular granules in Bi-fed biomass; salicylate-grown control granules lacked detected Bi.
The EDS beam spot exceeded granule diameter, so surrounding material contributes to the spectra.
This localization does not quantify total biomass uptake capacity or establish a unique Bi molecular/mineral phase.
